tools.name: ide_list
tools.description: List every VB6 IDE the hub can address: this machine (instance registry %TEMP%\vb6mcp\instances, then a port scan of 8766..8799 plus VB6MCP_PORT and HKCU\Software\VB6MCP\Port) AND each configured REMOTE endpoint (allow-list from VB6MCP_REMOTES / bridge/hub_remotes.json -- never discovered, listed with its probe status even when it does not answer). Reports faceSource (live|snapshot), the snapshot contractVersion/toolCount, per instance pid/port/project plus the ONE-set identity endpoint/remote/targetKey/pathVia, projectPathReal (canonical realpath) beside projectPathAsGiven (the spelling the registry published) and aliasAsGiven (the caller-supplied spelling that resolves to the same identity -- junction/alias spellings of one .vbp are ONE candidate, echoed in aliasEcho), the configured endpoints with their probe status, stale registry entries with a reason, and any conflict (two live IDEs publishing the same project identity on one endpoint). Read-only.

tools.name: ide_target
tools.description: Set or clear the default IDE target used when a tools/call has no _target. target = pid | project name | port | "auto" (any other string is stored verbatim and never matches). "auto" or "" CLEARS the default. Hub-local state only: the default is NOT a hard pin - a stored pid that is no longer live is IGNORED (receipt: staleDefaultPid/defaultIgnored/targetDiagnostic) and the documented target ladder picks instead.

target.description: pid, project name, port, or auto

tools.name: ide_start
tools.description: Start a VB6 IDE for the given project (.vbp), then WAIT FOR READINESS and say which part is proven: ok:true + started:true means the process was created; ready:true means the add-in was OBSERVED answering mcp_info for that pid within ready_wait_ms (default 15000, min 1000, max 180000). ready:false is a truthful timeout: the receipt carries readyWaitMs, readyChecks{registryVisible,transportUp,addInAnswers,projectMatches} and pollingHint, and the pid is still valid (poll ide_list for it). If that .vbp is already open on this machine the running instance is REUSED (started:false, reused:true, processesCreated:0) instead of starting a second one. Needs an explicit project or VB6MCP_AUTOSTART_PROJECT plus a resolvable VB6.EXE; otherwise a structured not_implemented / vb6_exe_not_found is returned.

ready_wait_ms.description: readiness poll budget in ms (default env VB6MCP_IDE_START_READY_MS or 15000; min 1000, max 180000). The poll observes the add-in; it is never a fixed sleep

tools.name: ide_stop
tools.description: Stop an IDE instance by pid. pid is REQUIRED (omitting it answers ok:false + reason=not_implemented). It only stops an instance this hub owns; otherwise it refuses with reason=not_allowed (ownershipBasis names why) or reason=foreign_instance_refused for a known port below 8767, and NOTHING is stopped.

pid.description: the pid to stop (required; as reported by ide_list)

tools.name: ide_restart
tools.description: RECOVER a wedged IDE by stopping OUR OWN instance and starting it again on the same project. Sequence: best-effort save_project -> graceful quit_ide -> confirm the process is gone (force kill only if it will not go) -> clear our own instances/<pid>.json registry entry -> start VB6.EXE on the same .vbp -> wait for the new instance -> prove three-way readiness (add-in answers, mcp_info answers, project matches). It NEVER stops an instance below port 8767: 8766 belongs to an EXTERNAL process on this machine (discipline 107). Every path returns the same key set: {ok,restarted,stoppedPid,newPid,port,project,targetSource,ownership,refused_reason,stopConfirmed,saveAttempted,saveOk,registryCleared,lockCleared,three_way_ok,threeWay,vb6Exe,vb6ExeSource,waitMs,instances,steps,note}. CONTINUABLE OPERATION (WP-22-02): the call waits at most wait_ms (default 25000, env VB6MCP_HUB_RESTART_WAIT_MS, min 1500) and then returns a PENDING receipt (ok:false + pending:true + state:"in_progress" + opId + currentStep + lastKnownState - a client-side request timeout is NOT this tool's answer and is NOT a failure). Continue it with ide_restart{opId:"..."}: that answers from the in-process operation registry (kept 30 minutes, NOT across a hub restart) and starts NOTHING. Every path carries opId/started/state(done|refused|error|in_progress)/finished/elapsedMs/currentStep/lastKnownState/opRule. A SECOND restart while one is in flight is refused with reason:"restart_in_progress" + inProgress{opId,...}, because a second restart could stop the process the first one just started; the oldest op is never replayed.

pid.description: The instance to restart (as reported by ide_list). Omit when exactly ONE instance is online.

project.description: The .vbp to restart the IDE on. Required unless the target instance reports its project path.

opId.description: Continue (poll) an operation that a previous ide_restart returned, e.g. from a PENDING receipt. With opId this call answers from the operation registry and starts NOTHING: pid/project/wait_ms are ignored. An unknown/expired opId refuses with reason:"op_not_found".

wait_ms.description: How long THIS call may block before it returns the pending receipt (default 25000, env VB6MCP_HUB_RESTART_WAIT_MS; clamped to 1500..300000). The restart itself KEEPS RUNNING in the background after a pending receipt, so a small wait_ms plus ide_restart{opId} is the non-blocking usage.

tools.name: ide_kill_and_relaunch
tools.description: HUB-side, add-in-INDEPENDENT reset for ONE VB6 IDE: stop the process, clear its registration, launch VB6.EXE on the same .vbp and poll until the add-in answers. This is the recovery primitive for a BUSY/WEDGED add-in pipe, where ide_state{release_inflight:true} cannot even be delivered because it travels the same pipe. Only an instance THIS hub owns (started by it, or its registration says startedByHub=true) is ever signalled; a known port below 8767 (including the reserved 8766) is REFUSED, and a remote-bridge instance is never touched. Every path returns: {pid, stoppedPid, newPid, port, ready, readyWaitMs, threeWay{http,mcpInfo,project}, three_way_ok, ownership, ownershipBasis, ownedByHub, stopConfirmed, registryCleared, projectVbp, pinPort, vb6Exe, steps[], elapsedMs, refused_reason, howToProceed, failureKind, suggestedAction, retrySafe}. ready:false after a relaunch means the process WAS started but the add-in had not answered within ready_wait_ms - poll ide_list for newPid.

pid.description: the instance to reset (as reported by ide_list). Required - this tool never guesses a target.

project.description: absolute .vbp to relaunch on; defaults to the project path the instance published in its registration (if it publishes none, the call is refused BEFORE anything is stopped).

ready_wait_ms.description: readiness poll budget in ms (default env VB6MCP_IDE_RELAUNCH_READY_MS or 60000; min 1000, max 300000). The poll observes the add-in; it is never a fixed sleep

tools.name: list_lessons
tools.description: List the VB6MCP lessons (experience library): scenario / trap / do with scope and enabled state.

tools.name: add_lesson
tools.description: Add or overwrite a lesson in the user layer (mcp_lessons/user.json), keeping a timestamped backup <user.json>.bak_<yyyymmdd_hhnnss>. scenario, trap and do are all REQUIRED (a call missing any of them fails with lesson_fields_required); id is optional (mints the first free custom-N) and an existing id is REPLACED IN PLACE. scope is stored verbatim (conventionally all | mcp | vb6; default all).

scope.description: all | mcp | vb6 (optional; stored verbatim, default all)

tools.name: delete_lesson
tools.description: Remove a user lesson, or disable a shipped one (writes enabled=false for a DEFAULT lesson). id is REQUIRED (an empty id fails with lesson_id_required; an unknown id answers ok:false + error=lesson_not_found); the receipt's action is removed | disabled(default) | not_found.

tools.name: export_lessons
tools.description: Export the merged lesson library as Markdown (re-importable via import_lessons_md, with the loss that the scope: and enabled:false lines are ignored on import - an imported lesson is always scope=all / enabled=true).

tools.name: import_lessons_md
tools.description: Import lessons from a Markdown file: a ## [id] scenario header plus trap:/do: body lines (the Chinese markers 坑:/应: are accepted too). An id that already exists in the MERGED library (shipped defaults included) is NEVER overwritten - it is counted in conflicts and a fresh custom-N id is minted for that lesson; a section without BOTH trap and do is skipped. dryRun:true parses and reports parsed/added/skipped/idsUsed/conflicts without writing.

dryRun.description: Parse only, do not write (default false)
